messages.author: d6f746729a48387e
messages.subject: fmesher won't run, requires glibc 2.14
parts:
Hi again Håvard and crew,

I've downloaded the latest INLA source and installed it from source on a Linux machine with glibc 2.19 installed. The package installs and loads fine, can run inla(), but fails when I try to use inla.mesh.create() and returns the following error message.

/home/cliffosj/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.14' not found (required by /home/cliffosj/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher)
/home/cliffosj/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/fmesher: /lib64/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.14' not found (required by /home/cliffosj/R/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu-library/3.2/INLA/bin/linux/64bit/libgsl.so.19)
Error in fmesher.read(prefix, "manifold") :
  File '/tmp/RtmplTQbxi/fmesher6e3d286b4b7e.manifold' does not exist.

I've contacted the IT support team for assistance with this, but just wanted to check if this was a known issue with fmesher on Linux systems.

If I can't get this problem solved, is there any way for creating a mesh on one system and transferring it to another so it can be loaded? I need to run multiple simulations with the same mesh and while I can use the data.dir option to tell R where to store a mesh, I can't seem to find instructions on whether inla.spde.create() or associated functions have a way to read in a mesh from a given file/folder.

Thanks,

Sam

messages.author: bbb9357156c132fe
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] fmesher won't run, requires glibc 2.14
parts:
Hi Sam,

The very pragmatic answer to the last part of your question (Finn can probably tell you what's going on, but I have no idea!) is that if you save the mesh variable  as a RData object you should be able to transfer it between machines (it's just a list of lists, so there's nothing machine dependent).  Just re-making the mesh may not be guaranteed to make the same mesh every time.

Again, someone else will probably have a better solution, but this is a quick one.

Best wishes,

Dan

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] fmesher won't run, requires glibc 2.14
parts:
You may have better luck building a package using the Makefile from here:
https://bitbucket.org/hrue/r-inla/src/70d490ec44b0f5bb79034a4c794e1280e9640c48/build-user/linux/Makefile?at=default&fileviewer=file-view-default

That should in theory let you build all the binaries, as well as the R package, on the machine that you need to to run it on, from the current bitbucket source. However, it may not have been tested for a while, and the build system might not be entirely in sync with it.

Ps. Meshes (and spde objects) can be saved in .rdata files, so can in principle be stored and reused, but functions like inla.spde.make.A() also call fmesher, so this might not help in this case.

Finn

INLA:::inla.dynload.workaround()

and then proceed, as this setup the static builds (with out the libR
support)
